title: SLO/SLI mapping and operational guardrails for geo-fallback, adaptive circuit breakers, and load-shedding
creator: Aisha Turner
description: This ticket captures the SLO/SLI definitions and the operational policy for automatic geo-fallback, adaptive circuit breakers, and load-shedding across model endpoints. Goal: produce a single runnable playbook + config knobs that platform engineers and reliability on-call can use to (1) reason about error budget burn, (2) safely trigger regional failover, (3) apply dynamic circuit-breaking, and (4) prioritize or degrade traffic to meet customer-facing latency/availability SLOs.
rationale: We have increasing cross-region tail latency and occasional regional networking failures causing cascading error budget burns. Current mitigation steps are ad-hoc (manual DNS, removing regions) and risk long outages or unnecessary capacity spend. Standardizing SLO attribution and automated guardrails will reduce toil and improve mean time to recovery.
sli_definitions:
- Request success rate (user-visible): proportion of requests that return a non-5xx response within timeout. Measurement window: 5m/1h/24h.
- Latency SLI: p95 and p99 server-side latency for final token emitted (end-to-end generation pipeline), per route.
- Cost-availability SLI: fraction of requests served by primary (fastest) model variant vs. fallback variants per region.
- Correctness SLI (select routes): semantic similarity pass rate against golden prompt set (nightly eval).
- Model-internal health: KV-cache hit ratio and batching efficiency (for ops use).
Notes: All SLIs are computed per endpoint-model pair and tagged by region. Aggregation windows: 1h for alerts, 24h for SLO reporting.
slo_targets_and_error_budget:
- High-priority product endpoints: 99.9% success within latency SLO (p95 < 220ms) -> monthly error budget 0.1%.
- Interactive chat endpoints: 99.5% success within p95 < 350ms -> monthly error budget 0.5%.
- Bulk embeddings: 99.0% success within p95 < 2s -> monthly error budget 1.0%.
Error budget policy:
- Burn rates computed per endpoint-model-region.
- Soft alert (ops): burn_rate > 2 for 30m -> notify on-call, add to incidence dashboard.
- Hard action: burn_rate > 5 for 15m -> trigger automated mitigation sequence (reduce non-critical traffic, enable fallback variants, tighten circuit breakers).
- Exhausted budget: if budget reaches 0.0 and remediation fails within 60m, escalate to exec on-call and consider capacity reallocation or temporary rate limit for self-serve customers.
circuit_breaker_policy:
- Inputs: instantaneous error rate (5xx), p99 latency, token queue depth, model GPU health.
- Thresholds (defaults): open if 5xx rate > 3% AND p99 latency > 2x SLO for 5m. Half-open after 2 minutes with a 1% pilot traffic injection.
- Adaptive scaling: CB threshold scales with baseline QPS and model tier. Low-traffic endpoints use conservative thresholds to avoid flapping.
- Actions when open: 1) route traffic to a compatible fallback model variant (same API semantics), 2) reduce max_tokens and beam counts, 3) apply per-customer soft-throttles following priority tiers.
- Circuit breaker metadata must be logged to tracing and correlated with error budget attribution for post-incident analysis.
failover_and_load_shedding_strategy:
- Tiered failover: prefer regional warm spares in same continent, then replica in secondary continent. Failover is traffic-sliced: 5%->20%->100% with success checks at each step.
- Progressive rollback: if secondary violates SLOs, roll back to primary but apply load-shedding rules.
- Load-shedding priority order: 1) background/batch jobs (drop first), 2) non-interactive streaming/long-token jobs, 3) interactive sessions degrade to compact model variant, 4) last-resort: global rate limit for low-tier customers.
- Degradation knobs: reduce response length, switch to quantized variant, disable non-essential post-processing (e.g., reranking).
- Cache considerations: ensure cache invalidation policy is aligned with failover (avoid serving stale long-lived KV entries after regional shift).
observability_and_alerting:
- Dashboards: per-endpoint SLI dashboard with error budget burn, regional comparison, and last 24h heatmap.
- Alerts:
  * Pager if high-priority endpoint burn_rate > 4 for 15m OR p99 latency exceeds 3x SLO for 10m.
  * Slack-only ops channel for burn_rate between 2-4.
- Tracing: include model variant, region, CB state, and cache hit ratio in span tags.
- Postmortem hygiene: any automated mitigation must create a post-incident ticket linking to playbook steps executed and metrics snapshots.
- SLI test harness: nightly synthetic traffic for top-20 endpoints across all regions to validate failover paths.
rollout_plan:
- Week 1: implement SLI computation per endpoint-model-region and expose dashboards (ENG + Observability).
- Week 2: prototype adaptive circuit breaker and simulation tests with replayed traffic (load-testing infra).
- Week 3: implement controlled geo-fallback orchestration with canary ramping and integrate KV-cache invalidation checks.
- Week 4: run chaos/DR test (induced region partition) and validate automated mitigation.
- Week 5: bake into on-call runbooks and train SRE rotation.
- Acceptance criteria: automated mitigations execute without human intervention in >= 90% of simulated failure scenarios and SLOs are restored to within 1.5x baseline within 20 minutes.

acceptance_criteria: SLIs defined and implemented as metrics in observability (per-endpoint-model-region).
Automated circuit breaker policy implemented and exercised under 3 simulated failure modes (CPU spike, network partition, model OOM).
Geo-fallback orchestration able to ramp to 100% in staged slices with rollback on SLO violation.
Runbook documented and integrated into on-call rotation; at least 2 SREs signed off after tabletop DR exercise.
open_questions: Should correctness SLI be enforced for all generation routes or only a curated subset?
What is the desired customer-facing messaging when an endpoint is degraded (SDK header, response field, status page)?
Do enterprise customers get automatic reserved capacity failover or should we always consult sales/legal before cross-region failover for region-restricted data?
decisions: Compute SLIs per endpoint-model-region (vs. global) to allow precise error budget attribution.
Use staged traffic ramp for region failover (5/20/100) with built-in telemetry checks before each step.
Implement adaptive circuit breaker with hysteresis and pilot traffic for half-open trials to reduce flapping.
